published_prior_art.cite: AllmanMatiasRhodes2009 establishes three-view recovery up to labels; ZhouTchetgenTchetgen2026 gives hidden binary-treatment causal identification.
BianZhouCui2026 Appendix A.8 constructs categorical inverse-feature product bridges and a valid influence function.

AllmanMatiasRhodes2009 proves mixture identifiability; Hu--Schennach/Deaner continuous array-decomposition work is a closer omitted comparison, but neither supplied source gives this stated bounded DQM lift.
ZhouTchetgenTchetgen2026 Theorem 2 gives the binary observed tangent-space characterization.
ZhouTchetgenTchetgen2026 supplies a binary infinite-dimensional orthocomplement and basis approximation, not the proposed fixed-K cell/conditional-Gram operator.
ZhouTchetgenTchetgen2026 pp. 61--62 gives only a discretization/basis approximation for continuous Y; no exact multilevel cell projector is given.
This is the Hilbert-space Pythagorean identity after Theorem 4 declares Q to be an orthogonal projector.
No checked source analyzes perturbation of this nested posterior/conditional-Gram pseudoinverse, but the asserted route is a standard finite-dimensional perturbation extension.
BianZhouCui2026 proves product-bridge remainder control in a different dynamic hidden-action model; the new projector-specific expansion is not verified there.
ZhouTchetgenTchetgen2026 and BianZhouCui2026 give asymptotic inference for related hidden-treatment/action scores, but not for the proposed exact projected K-class score.
It is a fixed-dimensional Gaussian/Slutsky consequence of Theorem 8 rather than a separate hidden-treatment frontier.
ZhouTchetgenTchetgen2026 Corollary 1 and p. 16 show that the binary-outcome binary-hidden-treatment orthocomplement vanishes and the displayed influence function is efficient.
The explicit K=3 regular witness is proposal-specific, though its downstream tangent and variance conclusions depend on the preceding new kernel.
BonhommeJochmansRobin2016 gives repeated-measurement mixture estimation, but not the specified one-fit derived-nuisance rate construction.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 and Open-ended Question 1
novelty_flags.one_line: The continuous array-decomposition comparison omits Hu and Schennach (2008) and Deaner (2023), which are closer published antecedents for full-law recovery with continuous proxy variables than several listed peripheral references.

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-density
soundness_flags.one_line: The standard-tag citation GuoOgburnShpitser2026 does not support the asserted uniform conditional-density envelope; its continuous discussion instead gives bridge-operator integrability/range conditions.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 5
soundness_flags.one_line: Once Q is an L2 orthogonal projector and phi-eff=phi-Qphi, both the variance equality and strictness iff are immediate Pythagoras, so this is a zero-substantive-step root target.

soundness_flags.label: ass:contrast-centering
soundness_flags.one_line: Theorem 5 quantifies over every c in R^K, so C1_K=0 is unused there; it is also not needed for fixed-q Gaussian inference in Theorem 9.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 8 and Open-ended Question 2
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The efficient limit theorem is conditional on coherent nuisance rates R_Sigma=o_P(1) and Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2); construction of a sieve fit attaining them remains open.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Efficient inference is claimed conditional on the displayed coherent-fit product rates, not as an unconditional nonparametric implementation theorem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 13--16, Theorems 2 and 4; pp. 61--62, Supplement S8.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies a hidden binary treatment, characterizes its observed tangent space, states that binary Y has zero correction, and for continuous Y defines the efficient projection as a limit of discretization/basis projections rather than a closed form.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 71--72, Appendix A.8, Assumption A.1 and equations defining q_a^X and g-bar_a
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For categorical latent actions the paper assumes nonsingular conditional moment matrices, constructs inverse-feature representations of latent-action indicators, multiplies them into product bridges, and states a valid observed-data influence function.

The continuous-model conditions displayed are compactness, square-integrability, and singular-system range conditions for bridge equations; the source does not state a uniform bound sup_{j,y,x} f_j(y|x)<=epsilon^{-1}.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:0809.5032v2 / Annals of Statistics 37(6A) primary-version equivalent text
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Three-view latent-class parameters are identifiable up to label swapping under the stated Kruskal-rank condition, with nonparametric component-measure identification under additional rank conditions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace Theorem 5 with an observable, non-tautological criterion for strict efficiency gain, for example a condition expressed through the recovered cell/Gram objects that certifies Qphi is nonzero on a scientifically named contrast class.
Add Hu and Schennach (2008) and Deaner (2023) to related work, then state precisely why their continuous full-law recovery does not supply the required measurable uniformly bounded DQM right inverse.
Retag ass:bounded-density as novel with a concrete application justification, or replace its citation with a source that actually uses the same uniform density envelope.
Make Proposition 11 an analytic worked K=3 certificate for the proposed operator, including exact lower bounds for the posterior and Gram gaps rather than numerical quadrature evidence alone.

recommended_next_step: Revise this angle: repair the unsupported standard tag, remove or strengthen the Pythagorean Theorem 5 root claim, and add the omitted continuous array-decomposition comparator chain before advancing.
